newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese banks to give 10 bln yuan in mortage loans.
newsitem.headline: Chinese banks to give 10 bln yuan in mortage loans.

text.p: China's state commercial banks will give about 10 billion yuan ($1.2 billion) in mortgage loans this year but the credits are unlikely to give the domestic real estate market much of a boost, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The newspaper said mortgage loans this year will be roughly in line with the total for 1996 which stood at 10.6 billion yuan. They will extend for as long as 20 years and cover up to 70 percent of housing costs.
The newspaper, published by the China Daily, quoted central bank researcher Zheng Yaodong as saying that interest in buying apartments being sold off by the state was rising.
However, it also quoted him as saying that new legislation being prepared to standardise mortgage lending would limit funding to buyers of apartments built with public funds.
Privately built homes will not qualify and that will limit the impact of mortgage lending on the real estate market, Zheng said.

China has moved cautiously in developing a mortgage lending market. It has been eager to sell off state owned housing where subsidies ensure that rents are so low that basic maintenance costs cannot be covered.
But it has also been concerned that mortgage lending would trigger another round of real estate speculation and lead to inflationary pressure. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
